summary: Checks whether a value is a number that is not negative.
description: `NaN` does not qualify: it is a number, but it is neither negative nor non-negative. The infinities behave as their sign suggests, so `Infinity` qualifies and `-Infinity` does not.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is a number that is not negative; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isNonNegative(0); // => true
isNonNegative(-0); // => true
isNonNegative(42); // => true
isNonNegative(Infinity); // => true
isNonNegative(-1); // => false
isNonNegative(NaN); // => false
isNonNegative("1"); // => false
```
